question.text: A leak proof cylinder of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>,</mo></math> made of a metal which has very low coefficient of expansion is floating vertically in water at <math><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> such that its height above the water surface is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math> When the temperature of water is increased to <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the height of the cylinder above the water surface becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>21</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The density of water at <math><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo></math> relative to the density at <math><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is close to:

solution.text:
According to Archemedes Principle, weight of the body is balanced by the upward thrust force due to buoyancy.

At 0°C, mg=A(100-20)ρ0°Cg, where A is area of cross-section of cylinder and ρ0°C is density of water at 0°C.
At 4°C, mg=A(100-21)ρ4°Cg, where ρ4°C is density of water at 4°C.
ρ4°Cρ0°C=8079=1.01
